The fastest land animal in the world is the cheetah.

Here is a budget plan for Alexis to upgrade his hiking gear for challenging multi-day treks. This plan assumes he is looking for high-quality, durable equipment that will last for years, focusing on performance and safety.

### **Budget Plan: High-End Hiking Gear Upgrade**

#### **1. Initial Investment Costs (One-Time Purchase)**

| Item | Description | Estimated Cost Range (USD) | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **High-Quality Hiking Boots** | Waterproof, ankle-supporting, Vibram sole, broken-in or break-in period required. | $150 - $250 | Brands like Salomon, La Sportiva, or Lowa. Essential for challenging trails. |
| **Durable Backpack** | 50-65 liter capacity, internal frame, hip belt, rain cover included. | $150 - $300 | Brands like Osprey, Gregory, or Deuter. Look for adjustable torso length. |
| **Lightweight Tent** | 2-person, 3-season, under 4 lbs, freestanding or semi-freestanding. | $200 - $400 | Brands like MSR, Big Agnes, or Nemo. Critical for multi-day comfort. |
| **Sleeping Bag** | Down or synthetic, rated for 20°F (-6°C) or lower. | $150 - $300 | Depends on climate; down is lighter, synthetic is better in wet conditions. |
| **Sleeping Pad** | Insulated inflatable or foam pad (R-value 3.0+). | $80 - $150 | Often overlooked but crucial for warmth and comfort. |
| **Total Initial Investment** | | **$730 - $1,400** | *Excludes clothing, food, and transport.* |

#### **2. Ongoing Costs (Per Trip or Annual)**

| Item | Description | Estimated Cost (USD) | Frequency |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Food & Water** | Dehydrated meals, snacks, water filtration/refills. | $15 - $25 per day | Per trip |
